brief: Hēni Te Kiri Karamu was born in 1840. Later in her life she was active in Māori concerns in Rotorua, where she died in 1933. She is best remembered as the compassionate heroine of the 1864 battle at Gate Pā on the outskirts of Tauranga. During a lull in the conflict, Hēni heard a cry for help from a mortally wounded British officer. She crept down to where the officer lay and gave him and some others water to drink. It was discovered later that the defendants had been exhorted with the text: “If thine enemy hunger, feed him: if he thirst, give him drink.”
